external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A grocery loyalty programme member who uses the mobile app, signs in, approves consent, collects points, and spends points on gift cards.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.
external_entities.notes: Members' phones are outside the system's cloud account.

external_entities.name: partner app
external_entities.description: A web application run by another company, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers
external_entities.notes: Partner apps are run on servers outside the organisation's control.

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application used by members to sign in, obtain access tokens, call the rewards API, and retain a refresh token.
processes.notes: The app's use of a PKCE challenge is not recorded.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The server that authenticates members, handles authorization-code flows and consent, issues tokens, and signs access tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
processes.notes: It signs tokens for the support console with the same key used for other tokens.

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API called by the mobile app and partner apps to read and write the points ledger.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
processes.notes: It checks JWT signatures with a public key downloaded at startup, but does not check client or audience.

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

processes.name: browser
processes.description: The browser used by a member to sign in and approve consent; it returns the authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
processes.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: The database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and closed-account state.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_stores.notes: Refresh tokens remain in the database after an account is closed.

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: The ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction
data_stores.notes: The ledger records which client made each change, but not which member approved it.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: The store receiving every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: Whether the app sends a PKCE challenge is not recorded.

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.data_description: points rewards requests and access token

data_flows.name: sign in browser
data_flows.description: A member signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

data_flows.name: authorize
data_flows.description: The browser submits the member's sign-in and consent interaction to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen
data_flows.notes: The consent screen lists the scopes.
data_flows.data_description: member sign-in, consent, and requested scopes

data_flows.name: request tokens
data_flows.description: The partner app sends token requests containing its client secret in the request body.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.data_description: client ID, client secret, authorization code, and token requests

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

data_flows.name: show points
data_flows.description: The partner app uses the rewards API to show a member's points.
data_flows.source_excerpt: such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points

data_flows.name: manage identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores and retrieves member identity, authorization, token, and consent data.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_flows.data_description: member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents

data_flows.name: read-write ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

data_flows.name: write requests
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes every received request, including headers, to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store

data_flows.name: take access tokens
data_flows.description: The support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.

trust_boundaries.name: own cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's own cloud account, where the authorization server, rewards API, support console, and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: members' phones
trust_boundaries.description: The members' phones, which are outside the organisation's cloud account and run the mobile app and browser.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: apart from the members' phones and the partner apps

trust_boundaries.name: partner servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers run by other companies for their partner apps.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.basis: The support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.basis: The support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.basis: The source states that the points ledger holds every member's balance and every points transaction.
